_comment: Golden vector for the audio OUTPUT STAGE of both implementations, so the two
can be compared without listening to them. The plugin (src/spyService.ts, the
ramp loop) and the standalone app (native-app/Sources/LocalRadio.swift level()
plus AudioSink.write) run the same three stages with the same constants:
per-mode makeup from MODE_MAKEUP / AudioLeveling.modeMakeup, an optional
output AGC that is off by default in both, and the tanh soft limiter at
0.85 x 32767, applied AFTER the volume in both. Every value below was
produced by running the real code, not by modelling it:
test/audioLeveling.test.ts checks the `plugin` arrays and
native-app/Tests/main.swift checks the `solo` arrays. They agree to within
int16 rounding, which is the only licensed difference — the plugin returns an
integer from softLimit and the app stays in float.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until 2026-09-10 the app applied the limiter BEFORE the
volume and the plugin applied it after, and nothing anywhere said so. That
fixes the knee at an input level instead of one that moves with the knob, so
identical settings on both sides came out quieter on the app: it compressed
peaks the plugin passed through linearly. At the 0.41 both were set to, the
app was 0.91 dB down at input 24000 — which is AM_AGC_MAX_OUTPUT, where the
carrier AGC's look-ahead puts peaks, so AM programme peaks landed there
routinely — and 3.52 dB down at full scale. It went unnoticed for two and a
half weeks because the app's audio stage only carried the sound once the app
became an independent receiver on 2026-09-10; before that the plugin was doing
the listening. Worse, the loudness difference it caused was first diagnosed as
a volume-knob difference and 'fixed' by turning the app DOWN from 0.9 to 0.41,
which matched the wrong one of the two.
So: two things a future change has to keep. The order is the same on both
sides, and this vector proves it for every input rather than for the one a
listener happens to notice. A topology change on either side turns these
arrays red, which is the point.

cases.name: vol041
cases.note: the volume both receivers are set to as of 2026-09-10; the limiter never reaches its knee here, so the whole vector is linear

cases.name: vol1
cases.note: no attenuation, so the limiter is well past its knee — the case that exercises the nonlinearity itself
